quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: One benefit of regular maintenance on your motorcycle is:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will continue to run like new. Regular maintenance checks should be part of your routine care.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of a lane?
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars build up in the center of each lane. It is usually still safe for a motorcycle to ride there unless the road is wet.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride faster to shake them off.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get ahead of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Riding faster only increases danger and may cause them to tailgate you at higher speed.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects you from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from injury in a crash and from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and stones thrown up by other vehicles.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are designed to:

options.text: Stop brakes from working on dry roads.
Tell you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.explanation: ABS prevents skidding and wheel lock-up during hard braking. When you apply maximum pressure to both brake controls, electronic sensors detect wheel lock and release and re-apply pressure to keep maximum braking power.

questions.question: If you think stopping will take longer than usual, you should:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, increase your following distance. If your motorcycle will take longer to stop, stay farther back from the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Try to squeeze into smaller traffic gaps.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and affects your motorcycle's handling. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more space to stop. Ride slower, start braking sooner, keep more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for larger gaps before turning or merging.

questions.question: An advantage to keeping a group of riders small is:

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
A small group can break traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always try to catch up to the group.
It is hard to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups are easier for other vehicles to pass, less likely to be separated by traffic or stop lights, and reduce pressure on slower riders to rush.

questions.question: It is best not to ride directly alongside another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may need to use the lane.
You cannot see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside a vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot and the driver cannot see you. The vehicle may also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have blind spots, but they are too small to worry about.
Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: A helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not block your side vision.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when needed, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch out for oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these have less grip.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after having one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and driving.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system and affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not fully cover your arms or legs.
Should not include a jacket in warm weather.
Can protect you during a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect you during a crash.
questions.explanation: The right clothing provides vital protection in a crash. Always wear a jacket and long pants that fully cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly so it doesn't flap but should not restrict your movement.

questions.question: Which of the following does not protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high ankle-supporting boots, and durable gloves for proper protection.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen often, so they are not a concern.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds under 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be fatal.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: To prevent injury on a slippery surface, a motorcyclist should:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, decrease your speed. Sudden moves can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not use the shoulder to escape a slippery road.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are not very important since motorcycles are small.
Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Should not be used if no vehicles are nearby.
Are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcyclist, you are vulnerable. Use your turn signals to alert others to your intentions. Always use them when changing lanes or turning, even if no one seems nearby.

questions.question: A good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to increase distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate at a higher speed, increasing danger.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
Three brakes: front, rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes. One brake controls the front wheel and one controls the rear wheel.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle operator should be ready for:

options.text: A parked car suddenly pulling out into traffic.
Other drivers seeing the motorcycle and staying clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car suddenly pulling out into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull out into traffic. Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space between your motorcycle and the parked cars.

questions.question: Which color helps you be seen the most?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green while riding. Bright clothing makes you easier to see at any time of day.

questions.question: What helps you be seen at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight at intersections. Position your motorcycle in the lane where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: For best protection, a helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly around your head with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.
